links.outcome: Readability of chatbot patient education responses versus 6th-8th grade target
links.effect: None of the models reached FRE above 60; DeepSeek-V3 most readable (FKGL about 6.5), others more complex than plain-language standards.
links.quote: None of the models reached a Flesch Reading Ease (FRE) score above 60, indicating that even the most readable outputs remained more complex than plain-language standards.

links.outcome: Plain-language comprehensibility of AI-generated patient education text
links.effect: No model reached FRE above 60; only DeepSeek-V3 met the 6th-8th grade target (FKGL about 6.5), and it scored lowest on reliability and quality.
links.quote: None of the models reached a Flesch Reading Ease (FRE) score above 60, indicating that even the most readable outputs remained more complex than plain-language standards.

unlisted_practices: Hybrid use of high-accuracy and high-readability chatbots with clinician oversight

screen.reason: Evaluates and compares the accuracy and readability of three commercial LLMs (ChatGPT-4o, Gemini 1.5 Flash, DeepSeek-V3) answering patient questions on rotator cuff tears without testing an organizational deployment safeguard.
